x: The "Poly" are fortunate, however, in having two such promising Juniors in their ranks as Stone and Denyer. Our sealed handicap held in conjunction provided our Walking Hon.

Individually, Bullock (Sheffield) had a lead of a yard from Stone (Polytechnic), but it was obvious that Surrey Walking Club had made certain of the team honours, thus breaking their run of three second team placings in past years.
So the "Met" gained a win; and we "took the honours." Redman (Met.) 29.59, H. Whitlock (Met.) 30.22, and Stone (Poly.) 30.30 headed the field.

One hundred and sixty-three competitors actually started to the signal of our President over our usual seven miles course, and from the start Johnson (Enfield), Cooper (Woodford Green), Redman (Metropolitan), Plumb (Enfield), Stone (Polytechnic) and Treacher, of ours, were prominent.

From the start Stone (Poly.) led, followed by the Surrey pair, and our two. It seemed that our two points lead was to be taken from us in this event, and we should be all-square on the competition total, leaving the One Mile race to be the deciding event.

He was forced to yield to Cooper and Stone before the end was reached, but this effort of Harry's must rank as one of his best. Tommy Green, young as ever, and Len Fletcher, who we were all glad to see on the road once again, and Bill Treacher, completed our team.

Our team was only a further five points away, and as our fourth man actually finished in front of Woodford's fourth, the keen nature of the struggle for team honours can easily be realised. Individually, Stone, of the Poly. Harriers, defeated our Harry Churcher by a yard, with A.
Jones (B), 38ft. 7; (2) Stone (T), 33ft. 2; (3) Moreton (T), 32ft. 4. 880 Yards Match.—(1) King (T); (2) Jarlett (B); (3) Peckett (T).
Discus.—(1) Morton (T.C.C.), 105ft. 8½; (3) Brewer (B), 103ft. 0½; (4) Jeal (B), 99ft. 11. Long Jump (1) Stone (T.C.C.), 20ft. 9; (3) T.
Young "Rodney" Stone, a regular chip off the old block, competed in both sprint races, and although running very green, he showed plenty of "guts" and was credited with a place in each.

At the end of the first lap, Stone of Dorking St. Pauls was away out in front and then came two Surrey A.C. runners followed by Len Herbert and a bunch of five Belgrave runners, and at this stage of the race it looked a walk-over for us.
Ches Walker went off first for us and he beat Stone of Dorking and Martin of Walton A.C. to give Jack Bragginton a useful lead, and his time of 14 mins. 12 secs. beat the previous course record.

Stone, the holder, was leading, but Ches Walker was close behind and, moreover, was running very easily, and it was obvious that unless Stone could get away from his opponent on the second lap of the country he had had it!

George Checkley who had started off at a very fast pace, second to Thompson, began to lose ground and when Crawley was reached had dropped back to fourth place, Vic Stone having gone up to 2nd and the Italian Resta 3rd.
Walker went off first for us and he beat Stone of Dorking and Martin of Walton AC to give Jack Braggington a useful lead, and his time of 14:12 beat the previous course record.
